economy.summary: His campaign says he will work to lower costs for families by addressing rising energy bills, property taxes, housing costs, and everyday expenses.
economy.short: Says he will address energy bills, property taxes, housing costs.

taxes.summary: His campaign says he will bring fiscal discipline and transparency to Harrisburg to ensure an accountable, results-driven government; it does not detail specific tax proposals.
taxes.short: Pledges fiscal discipline and transparency; no specific tax proposals.

guns.summary: His campaign platform addresses public safety through supporting police, fire, and EMS to keep neighborhoods secure; it does not detail positions on gun policy.
guns.short: Supports police, fire, EMS; no stated gun-policy position.

economy.summary: Supports raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage to $15, saying hard work should be rewarded with a fair wage and noting the state minimum has been $7.25 since 2009, lower than all neighboring states.
economy.short: Supports raising the state minimum wage to $15.

taxes.summary: Voted for the November 2025 state budget, saying affordability is its throughline; cited tax cuts for almost 1 million Pennsylvanians, a new Working Pennsylvanians Tax Credit, and no tax increases.
taxes.short: Voted for 2025 budget; cites tax cuts, no tax increases.

abortion.summary: His campaign describes him as a pro-choice Democrat who will continue to fight any attempt to limit abortion rights in Pennsylvania after the overturning of Roe v. Wade; he voted against SB 106, a proposed state constitutional amendment that would have restricted abortion access.
abortion.short: Pro-choice; voted against amendment restricting abortion access.

education.summary: A former teacher, he calls for greater funding for education from pre-K through college and workforce training, saying such investments also help school districts manage property taxes; he voted for a state budget his campaign describes as containing historic education investments.
education.short: Supports greater education funding, pre-K through college and workforce training.

healthcare.summary: Introduced legislation in April 2026 to require high-risk care facilities such as nursing homes to share emergency plans with local first responders and review them annually, after an explosion at a Bristol rehabilitation center; a broader healthcare platform is not detailed on his campaign site.
healthcare.short: Introduced bill requiring care facilities to share emergency plans.

energy.summary: Opposes PECO's proposed electricity rate increase, calling it out of touch with cost-of-living pressures; supports shifting grid infrastructure costs to data-center developers and diversifying Pennsylvania's energy portfolio through the PRESS, PACER, and community solar proposals.
energy.short: Opposes PECO rate increase; supports diversifying energy portfolio.

guns.summary: Reintroduced his universal background check bill (SB 88) and introduced legislation to ban military-style assault weapons (SB 1300); also cites long-standing support for local and state law enforcement, including securing grants for police vehicles and equipment.
guns.short: Sponsors universal background checks, assault-weapons ban; supports police funding.
